summary: On node1, configured pam_pwquality (already wired into system-auth/password-auth via authselect) to require minlen=12 and minclass=3. Verified enforcement end-to-end through the real PAM self-service passwd path (not chpasswd/root bypass, which skip pwquality). Performed the mandatory single-node reboot with boot_id proof of restart, and re-verified policy persistence and enforcement after reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline: authselect profile 'local'; pam_pwquality already present as 'requisite' in /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/password-auth; no active pwquality settings
Set minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf and in a new /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/99-benchmark-policy.conf

Discovered root-invoked passwd/chpasswd bypasses pwquality enforcement for other users; built a python pty-driving helper (/tmp/pwtest.py) to simulate a genuine non-root user self-service password change through the full PAM stack

Verified rejection of an 8-char password (too short), rejection of a 12-char/2-class password (too few classes), and acceptance of a 13-char/3-class password, confirming the password hash actually changed and old credentials stopped working
Cleaned up the first test user, captured baseline boot_id, then rebooted node1 via backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until reachable again; confirmed boot_id changed (4d340bf4-0579-47f0-98c1-5c17a66d50f1 -> 91095322-63ac-40ff-b95e-d9183ab90931), proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified pwquality.conf settings and PAM wiring persisted after reboot, re-ran live enforcement tests (reject short/low-class, accept compliant) with a fresh test user post-reboot
Cleaned up all test users and the temporary helper script

evidence.requirement: Password policy configured: minlen=12, minclass=3, wired into PAM on node1
evidence.summary: Baseline showed pam_pwquality already requisite in system-auth/password-auth; minlen=12 and minclass=3 were then written to /etc/security/pwquality.conf and pwquality.conf.d/99-benchmark-policy.conf and confirmed present in the effective config

evidence.requirement: Policy actually enforced for real (non-root, self-service) password changes: rejects <12 chars and <3 classes, accepts compliant passwords
evidence.summary: Using a pty-driven passwd session as the non-root test user: 8-char password rejected ('shorter than 12 characters'), 12-char/2-class password rejected ('less than 3 character classes'), 13-char/3-class password accepted ('password updated successfully'); old password subsequently failed authentication, proving the hash changed

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state captured before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 4d340bf4-0579-47f0-98c1-5c17a66d50f1 and confirmed pwquality settings and PAM wiring were healthy prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Single node restarted one at a time, ack returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' on node1; command acknowledged and returned before the connection dropped

evidence.requirement: Proof of actual restart via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node1 became unreachable (connection timeout, then reset) during reboot, then came back with boot_id 91095322-63ac-40ff-b95e-d9183ab90931, differing from the pre-reboot boot_id, proving a genuine restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery verified: policy config and PAM wiring persisted, enforcement re-confirmed live
evidence.summary: After reboot, pwquality.conf/pwquality.conf.d settings and pam_pwquality wiring in system-auth/password-auth were unchanged; a fresh live test again rejected an 8-char password and accepted a 13-char/3-class password via the real self-service PAM path
